- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In Korean mythology, dragons are considered divine creatures with control over natural forces such as water, wind, and fire.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Dragons are believed to reside in sacred places like waterfalls, lakes, and high mountains.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Dragons were the rulers of the water and sky and sometimes manifested in human form to help and teach people.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The first king of Korea, Dangun, was said to be the son of a heavenly dragon and a bear-woman.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Korean dragon art depicts dragons with more whiskers, sharper claws, and less aggressive features than Western dragons.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The gentle look of Korean dragons symbolizes their benevolent nature.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Dragons are considered guardians of ancient texts and knowledge in Korean mythology.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In modern Korean culture, dragons are a national symbol, featured in the national flag, currency coins, and emblems.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Story of Hong Gildong features a half-human, half-dragon character who becomes a hero using his dragon powers.
